implementation_notes: Kotlin's `data class` reduces the boilerplate half of the scatter but not its type duplication, and `copy()` actively encourages it: adding a field is non-breaking for construction but silently changes `copy()` call sites that expected the old value. The idiomatic consolidation is to keep one domain data class per concept and stop copying the same shape into a DTO, a screen state class and a form class. `sealed interface` on the set of variants is the counter for the switch-shaped variant of the same smell, since adding a subtype becomes a compile error at every exhaustive `when`.
idiom_name: data class + copy() calls spread across every consumer
pitfalls: `copy()` silently defaults a newly added field, so a call site that should set it does not.
A `when` without an `else` on a sealed type is exhaustive and gives a compile error — that property disappears the moment you switch to a plain class or an `Any` type.
`@Serializable` couples the scatter to the wire format, so a refactor is a breaking change to every consumer.
